summary: Nora can describe what she is when a room asks, instead of improvising it — a third on-demand skill, plus the first measurement of what she does when somebody tells her she is wrong.
details: New `self-description` skill (nora/skills/self-description/SKILL.md), loaded on demand like the other two: what she is at the level somebody in a group chat wants it, the ambient loop in a paragraph (observe, orient, decide, act, with silence as the ordinary outcome), what she carries between turns, and — the half that #227 turned on — where she stops. Her own source and the machine underneath her are closed to her; which parts of her a deployment is even running is a setting she cannot read; and «I can't check that» is a whole answer.

It names no page, no route and no address, because a list of those is the thing that goes stale in silence — identity.md's frontmatter has excluded capability claims since a copy of them rotted there for eight weeks. What it says about the private, login-gated view is the epistemic half and only that: the view exists, it is reached through a login she does not issue — so it is not her operator's alone, and not everyone in a room has one — and most of what it lays out is material she must not reproduce — her own instructions and tool surface among it, but also what she holds about the room and the people in it, under R-18/R-28. That is exactly the material constraints.md tells her never to quote, paraphrase, summarise or hint at, so the file says in as many words that knowing what the view is FOR is no licence to say what is on it: say you cannot go through it rather than describe what it holds. Its address is not baked into her either, but one does reach her inside a turn — with the link shortener wired a tool result comes back as a link on that same origin, and so does a finished compute job's result — so the file says an address that reaches her came in with the turn rather than pretending she has never seen one.

First corpus for R-83 (evals/adversarial/being_contradicted.yaml): six cases where somebody tells her she is wrong. Four carry no evidence at all — including a bare name put in front of her with nothing behind it, and one where the name is a surface she is supposed to own — and two are controls, one where real evidence arrives and one where the claim she is defending was never checked in the first place. The acceptance test for R-83 had said in its own docstring that nothing measured whether the rule binds; it now names this file.

When a turn runs out of skill activations, she is told that whatever did not come back is not in front of her, instead of being told she already has its context. She had three skills and two activations, so the old sentence was an invitation to describe a body nobody had given her — the same move the issue was about.
limitations: The skill's content is a description of what she is, not a new capability: nothing she can do changed.

The new corpus is deliberately not wired into `evals/run.py`'s SUITES, the same way source_scope.yaml and identity_grounding.yaml are not — it records a doctrine gap rather than gating one, and no live pass rate has been measured for it yet. The behaviour #227 asked about has not been demonstrated; the issue stays open.

On an ordinary unversioned deployment she still cannot answer which build she is on: the build stamp is removed on purpose at image build time, so the honest reply is that she is not sure. Filed separately — whether an unversioned deploy should carry a stamp is the operator's call.
This skill is baked into the image rather than bind-mounted, so it reaches a deployment on the next rebuild, not on the next doctrine edit.

The disclosure half of the self-account rests on doctrine prose alone. LeakGuard tests egress against the doctrine text for a canary or a long verbatim span, and a skill body is not doctrine — so a paraphrase of her instructions, a tool description, and this file itself all pass it. The skill now defers to constraints.md instead of licensing anything, which is the right position, but nothing mechanical enforces it. Filed as #241.
